title: Shabana Azmi, Marco Müller Set for Inaugural Kathmandu Film Festival
description: Veteran Indian actor Shabana Azmi and film critic and historian Marco Müller are among the guests at the first Kathmandu Film Festival (KFF), which
body:
Veteran Indian actor Shabana Azmi and film critic and historian Marco Müller are among the guests at the first Kathmandu Film Festival (KFF), which runs Oct. 30–Nov. 1 in Nepal.

	Launched by Kathmandu Metropolitan City, the three-day event will screen 40 films from 14 countries across several strands: the International Panorama, Nepal Panorama Shorts, a program of restored Nepali features and open-air screenings. Filmmakers and artists from around Asia are also due to attend. The city, a UNESCO Creative City of Film, set up the festival to showcase Nepali and international independent cinema and to build cultural ties.
	

	Marine Atlan’s Cannes premiere “La Gradiva” is among the international selections, as is Shahrbanoo Sadat’s “No Good Men,” which debuted in Berlin this year.

	“The international panorama is a curated showcase of global, contemporary and independent cinema that represents powerful stories, unique voices and distinct cultural perspectives,” said Ramyata Limbu, KFF’s artistic director. “The Nepal panorama shorts feature diverse and compelling stories about Nepal by emerging local talent.”

	Nepal’s film history gets a section of its own. A retrospective of restored titles from the 1970s and 1980s includes “Kumari,” credited as the country’s first color feature.

	Yamagata, Japan, which holds the same UNESCO film designation as Kathmandu, is the focus of a separate shorts program. Organizers tied the showcase to the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Nepal and Japan, and said it is meant to deepen links between the two cities.
	

	Events are spread across venues including Basantapur, City Hall, the Nepal Tourism Board, Jai Nepal Cinema and Taragaon. Alongside the films, the lineup takes in a heritage walk, master classes and conversations with filmmakers, with prizes to be handed out in the youth video challenge and Nepal panorama sections. Screenings are free, though some events require booking ahead.

	“Kathmandu is not just the city of its indigenous communities, whose culture and heritage are at its heart. It is also a city shaped by people from every corner of Nepal,” said Sunita Dangol, Kathmandu’s acting mayor. “Over generations, communities from across the country have brought their traditions, languages, art, music and stories to Kathmandu. That coming together is what makes this city so vibrant and unique.”

	Organizers are pitching KFF as a festival for the general public, one that links the city’s heritage with present-day cinema and the global film community.

	“Nepal has been through a profound tragedy with the floods, and in moments like these, stories become even more important,” Dangol said. “They help us make sense of what we have experienced, connect with one another, heal and find the courage to move forward.”

schema.headline: Shabana Azmi, Marco Müller Set for Inaugural Kathmandu Film Festival

title: California Begins Discussion on Unlimited Film Incentives: ‘That Is a Heavy Lift’
description: California lawmakers began a discussion Thursday about removing the cap on the state’s $750 million incentive for film and TV production, while ack
body:
California lawmakers began a discussion Thursday about removing the cap on the state’s $750 million incentive for film and TV production, while acknowledging that such a move would face budget hurdles.

	At an Assembly committee hearing in North Hollywood, a handful of state lawmakers heard testimony from union leaders and industry advocates who argued that the program — which was doubled last year — is not enough to stop the outflow of production jobs.
	

	Betsy Beers, the creative partner of Shonda Rhimes, told the committee that she had hoped to shoot a new “Grey’s Anatomy” spinoff in Santa Clarita. But the show, which is set in West Texas, did not get a California tax credit.

	“We lost a lot of time, and a lot of money, and now we are filming in Albuquerque,” Beers said. “We want to be here.”

	Because the state incentive is capped, projects must apply during periodic windows and then compete with other shows on a “jobs ratio” score. Beers said the show lost out initially because it didn’t get score highly enough. When ABC tried again in the fall, the program was already oversubscribed and was no longer taking applications.

	“The program is still not competitive or predicable enough to address the loss of production to other regions,” said Arlen Valdivia, vice president of state government affairs at the Motion Picture Association. “There needs to be more done to make California competitive.”

	FilmLA, the permitting agency, reported last week that production volume continues to fall in the Los Angeles area, even as the share of scripted TV shows receiving a state subsidy has nearly doubled. Several speakers at Thursday’s hearing called for eliminating the $750 million cap entirely — saying the limit leaves producers uncertain about whether they will get the credit.
	

	Georgia’s credit has no limit and New York’s allows the state to pull from allocations for future years — amounting to an uncapped credit. Rick Chavez Zbur, who chairs the Assembly Select Committee on Growing and Retaining the Creative Economy in California, said he expects to make improvements in the next legislative session.

	“I want to try to do our best to make whatever changes we can, and I think either increasing the cap or eliminating it,” Zbur said after the hearing. “But you know that is a heavy lift. But we’re going to try this year to make as much progress as we can.”

	Lawmakers are also dealing with a structural deficit and deep cuts to Medicaid — which has intensified competition for tax dollars.

	During the hearing, Zbur floated the idea of “dynamic scoring” — suggesting that the state should account for the benefit from the film credit instead just looking at the headline cost. That idea, he said, would be key to persuading lawmakers that an unlimited credit is a worthwhile investment.

	“The way we’re looking at the return needs to be what we’re focused on,” said John Harabedian, another member of the committee. “It becomes a regional fight. It becomes a best-use-of-a-dollar fight… The numbers are going to convince our colleagues that don’t necessarily live in L.A.”

	Rowan Isaaks, an economist with the state Legislative Analyst’s Office, cited research showing that film credits return 20-50 cents for every dollar invested by the state. He also expressed skepticism about dynamic scoring. “It’s subject to a lot of uncertainty,” he said.

	Stephen Cheung, the president of the Los Angeles Economic Development Committee, cited his own group’s research, which found a return of $1.07 to state and local coffers. That report was funded by the MPA.

	Assemblyman Nick Schultz floated the idea of extending the expiration date of the state program, which is currently set to sunset in 2030, as a way of offering greater certainty to productions. He and other also suggested providing a subsidy for above-the-line costs — salaries for actors, directors, etc. — and opening up eligibility for the program to commercials and game shows.

	“Why should we be picking and choosing?” he asked. “Why should we be picking winners and losers? Let’s incentivize all of it to stay.”
	

	The state raised the base credit from 20% to 35% last year, while increasing the overall cap from $330 million to $750 million.

	“The higher credit might mean fewer projects overall,” Isaaks noted. “There’s a possibility that the more generous our credit is, the fewer productions we can fund in total.” 

	Since Gov. Gavin Newsom expanded the state incentive last year, lawmakers have added additional measures to bolster it. The Legislature created a $10 million incentive for post-production and passed a bill to expedite studio rebates and exempt credits for independent films from a $5 million credit cap.

	While Congress is considering a 20% nationwide incentive, several speakers argued that even if that passes, California will still face stiff competition from other states.

	“We should not assume the work will return because federal policy changes,” said Lindsay Dougherty, leader of the Hollywood Teamsters.

schema.headline: California Begins Discussion on Unlimited Film Incentives: ‘That Is a Heavy Lift’

title: Matthew Weiner Exits Peacock, 101 Studios Series ‘The Chairman’ Starring Eddie Murphy (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Matthew Weiner is no longer involved with the drama series “The Chairman” that is currently in development at Peacock, Variety has learned exclusiv
body:
Matthew Weiner is no longer involved with the drama series “The Chairman” that is currently in development at Peacock, Variety has learned exclusively from sources.

	The project was first reported to be in the works at the streamer less than a month ago, with Eddie Murphy attached to star. According to sources, creative differences between Weiner and the show’s producers caused them to part ways. 


	A new showrunning team is already said to be in place and will be announced in the coming days. The show’s writers’ room has been placed on a two-week hiatus as the new creative leads come onboard. 
	

	Exact plot details for “The Chairman” remain under wraps. Should it get picked up to series, it would be the first live-action series in which Murphy has starred since his days as a cast member on “Saturday Night Live.” 

	The series will be produced by Universal Television and 101 Studios, which is run by “Yellowstone” executive producer David Glasser. 101 is currently under a first-look film and television deal at NBCUniversal that began in January. “The Chairman” will also be the first project to come out of ex-Paramount boss Chris McCarthy’s deal at NBCUniversal, which was first reported in November 2025 and put him in a consulting role on the studio’s relationship with Glasser and 101. Murphy serves as a producer “The Chairman” in addition to starring. 

	Weiner is best known for creating the seminal TV drama “Mad Men,” which aired for seven seasons on AMC and won 16 Emmy Awards. “The Chairman,” assuming it is to be greenlit, would have marked Weiner’s first TV writing credit since 2018, when he created the Amazon Prime Video series “The Romanoffs.”

schema.headline: Matthew Weiner Exits Peacock, 101 Studios Series ‘The Chairman’ Starring Eddie Murphy (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Beef’ Actor Justin H. Min’s ‘Journey There,’ Hong Sangsoo’s Locarno Winner ‘Nowhere to Lay My Eyes’ Rack Up International Sales for Finecut
description: Hong Sangsoo’s “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” a triple prizewinner at the 79th Locarno Film Festival, and Kim Jin-yu’s “Journey There,” the first Korean
body:
Hong Sangsoo’s “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” a triple prizewinner at the 79th Locarno Film Festival, and Kim Jin-yu’s “Journey There,” the first Korean production to star “Beef” actor Justin H. Min, have picked up a new batch of territory deals through Seoul-based sales outfit Finecut.

	For “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” Carlotta Films has taken France, Mimosa Films has Japan, Kligger has Argentina and The Stone and the Plot has Portugal. The new pacts add to earlier sales to The Cinema Guild for North America, Filmgarten for Austria, Hugoeast for China, Atalante for Spain, Cola Films for Taiwan and the Institute of Contemporary Arts for the U.K.
	

	The film is Hong’s 35th feature. At Locarno it won best direction, best performance and the Ecumenical Jury Prize. It sees the director team up again with regulars Kim Minhee (“By the Stream”) and Kwon Haehyo (“What Does That Nature Say to You”), and marks his first outing with Choi Myeonggil, whose credits include TV series “Durian’s Affair.” Jeonwonsa Film Co. produced.

	“Journey There” has sold to Andrews Film for Taiwan, KDDI Corporation for Japan, Lev Cinema for Israel and Izagur Media for Mongolia, while Kairos Distribution acquired inflight rights. The drama centers on a middle-aged widow who begins getting ready for her own journey and gets drawn into relationships she never saw coming in the apartment she has just moved into.

	Min’s credits include Kogonada’s “After Yang” and the Netflix series “Beef” and “The Umbrella Academy.” The film is the second feature from Kim, whose first, “Bori,” took two prizes at the 24th Schlingel International Film Festival. Kim’s own company, Pado, produced.
	

	“Journey There” was released in Korea on Oct. 28. It has been invited to the Moscow International Film Festival, the New York Asian Film Festival and, more recently, the Paris and London Korean film festivals.

	Fresh from Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market, Finecut heads to AFM with a slate that includes the animated “Long Long Night.” The film will screen there for buyers for the first time in its English-dubbed version. It also has invitations from Toronto, Busan and Sitges under its belt.

	Also on offer are “Dora,” selected for Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight and Busan’s Gala Presentation section, and “Wi-Fi Love in the Palace,” a period fantasy romance toplined by Kim Young-hoon of K-pop group The Boyz.

schema.headline: ‘Beef’ Actor Justin H. Min’s ‘Journey There,’ Hong Sangsoo’s Locarno Winner ‘Nowhere to Lay My Eyes’ Rack Up International Sales for Finecut

title: Earl Barret, TV Writer and Co-Creator of ‘Too Close for Comfort,’ Dies at 94
description:
Comedy writer Earl Barret died in his home in Sherman Oaks, California, on Oct. 22. He was 94.

	Barret began his career in TV writing in 1961 afte
body:
Comedy writer Earl Barret died in his home in Sherman Oaks, California, on Oct. 22. He was 94.

	Barret began his career in TV writing in 1961 after taking Robert C. Dennis’s weekly free TV writing class. The two would go on to write episodes for several shows together.

	Over the next 30 years, Barret wrote on over 30 shows, including “My Favorite Martian,” “Batman,” “Bewitched,” “The Andy Griffith Show,” “I Spy,” “The Partners,” “Sanford and Son” and “Welcome Back, Kotter.” His biggest hit was “Too Close for Comfort,” the show he created, wrote and executive produced with longtime writing partner Arne Sultan. He also served as the director of 13 episodes of the series.
	

	“Too Close for Comfort” ran on ABC from 1980 to 1983 before being broadcast across several stations from 1984 to 1987. Starring Ted Knight, Nancy Dussault and Jim J. Bullock, the log-line for the series reads: “In liberal San Francisco, a conservative cartoonist tries to keep his two daughters, who rent an apartment below him, safe.”

	In addition to TV writing, Barret, with Sultan, wrote plays and the feature film “See No Evil, Hear No Evil.”

	Before becoming a writer, Barret pursued a career in acting and had a SAG card. He graduated from Hollywood High and Los Angeles City College. His daughter, J.K. Barret, describes him as a “lifelong learner with a keen, curious mind and a gift for impeccable comic timing. He spent nine decades cultivating his passion for the performing arts, music and entertainment that began with the tap dancing and violin lessons he took in childhood in Canton, Ohio.”
	

	He is survived by his wife, Barbara Barnett Barret; daughter, J.K. Barret; son, John Nelson; and five grandsons. He was preceded in death by daughter, Lisa Nelson.

schema.headline: Earl Barret, TV Writer and Co-Creator of ‘Too Close for Comfort,’ Dies at 94

title: Joseph Mazzello Leads Cecil Hotel Horror ‘A Grim Life,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles
body:
Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel. 

	Hong Kong outfit Cappu Films has picked up international sales, it was unveiled at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market.

	Francesco Lucente writes and directs. Mazzello, whose credits also take in “The Pacific,” plays Tom, a filmmaker down on his luck who pays the bills scrubbing toilets and can’t stop reworking the one script he has. A friend steers him toward “Böse,” a lost silent picture from 1931, and Tom’s hunt for an artistic breakthrough pulls him toward a dark secret.
	

	Max Beesley (“Jack Ryan”) plays producer Joe, with Wes Studi (“Avatar: Fire and Ash”) as Nic, Carl Lumbly (“Captain America: Brave New World”) as Henry and Arnetia Walker (“Bookie”) as Chelsea. Studi is a 2019 recipient of an Academy Honorary Award.

	The building itself does much of the work. The film draws its scares from the hotel’s hallways and concealed rooms, leaning on sound, shadow and Tom’s deepening isolation to tighten the dread.

	Lucente also produces. The project will move into pre-production in December 2026 ahead of a January 2027 shoot, with delivery penciled for July 2027.

	“‘A Grim Life’ is a deeply personal project for me, one that explores the darker side of ambition, obsession, and the sacrifices we make in pursuit of our dreams,” Lucente said. “The Cecil Hotel provides an extraordinary and haunting backdrop for a story where the boundaries between reality and the supernatural begin to disappear.”
	

	Cappu first presented the film to buyers in Busan and is keeping those conversations going before cameras roll. Janice Woo of Cappu Films said the Cecil Hotel and the lost film give the project an immediately compelling premise, “while Tom’s desperation gives the story its emotional center.” She added: “Following our work with Francesco on ‘Starbright,’ we’re pleased to continue the relationship with a project that brings together a distinctive atmosphere and an experienced cast.”

	Lucente previously directed the drama “Badland” and the fantasy “Starbright,” which stars Ted Levine, John Rhys-Davies and Diego Boneta.

	Besides “Starbright,” the Cappu slate carries another Lucente fantasy, “Sinbad,” plus the action titles “Lion Fist” and “Red Bird.” The company’s catalog spans horror, fantasy, action and arthouse fare, and also includes TV series and library titles from Hong Kong cinema’s Golden Era.

schema.headline: Joseph Mazzello Leads Cecil Hotel Horror ‘A Grim Life,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: French Action Film ‘Red Bird’ Lands CIS Deal as D.C. Romance ‘Step Back, Doors Closing’ Bows at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)
description: A French action film and an American indie romance are both up for grabs with international buyers at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFC
body:
A French action film and an American indie romance are both up for grabs with international buyers at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market. 

	Cappu Films has sold “Red Bird” to Kinologistika LLC for the CIS region, which covers Russia and other former Soviet states, and has taken on international sales for “Step Back, Doors Closing.”

	“Red Bird” is directed by Alexandre Laugier, Thomas Habibes and Houssam Adili, who draw on backgrounds in stunt work and martial arts. Habibes and Adili also take the lead roles, with Eric Delcourt, Jean-Louis Tribes and Jean-Marie Paris in support. The story follows Max, whose father worked covertly as Red Bird. When the older man dies in unexplained circumstances, Max and his friend Sam set out to learn the truth, and the search leads them into a perilous plot.
	

	Shot in Marseille and made independently, the film puts physical action front and center. SOUTHfilms produced it and released it in French cinemas in January.

	“‘Red Bird’ brings the energy of its filmmakers and stunt team directly to the screen. We’re pleased to have secured a CIS deal and look forward to introducing the film to more distributors in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.



	

					“Step Back, Doors Closing”
									Cappu Films
	



	“Step Back, Doors Closing” is written and directed by Carter Ward, who produced with Jane Hollon and Kathryn Crabtree. Carmen Berkeley and Reilly Walters lead the cast in the story of Ryan and Julisa, a pair of strangers who cross paths on a Washington, D.C. Metro train. Across 24 hours, they roam the city and open up about what they want and what scares them as a romance takes hold. Michelle Macedo, Ashley Romans and Mershad Torabi co-star.
	

	The film bowed at Los Angeles’ Dances With Films in 2024. Freestyle Digital Media has released it in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean, and Cappu is looking for partners in other territories.

	“I could not be more proud or excited to partner with Cappu Films. Their support means the world not only to myself, but our entire cast and crew. We can’t wait for international audiences to see the version of Washington, D.C. we know and love. One where meet-cutes are still possible, and single weekends can change the trajectory of our lives forever,” said Ward of Arden Pictures.

	Cappu Films works with independent filmmakers on both arthouse and commercial titles. Its library spans action, horror, fantasy and arthouse fare, TV series and classics from Hong Kong cinema’s golden era.

schema.headline: French Action Film ‘Red Bird’ Lands CIS Deal as D.C. Romance ‘Step Back, Doors Closing’ Bows at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Ian McKellen Pays Tribute to Close Friend Patrick Stewart: ‘He Wore His Heart on His Sleeve’
description: Ian McKellen wrote a moving tribute to Patrick Stewart, his close friend of many years, following his death Thursday at age 86 after suffering from
body:
Ian McKellen wrote a moving tribute to Patrick Stewart, his close friend of many years, following his death Thursday at age 86 after suffering from Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia.

	“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” McKellen wrote on Instagram.
	

	“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in ‘Star Trek’. “But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk — getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?” Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theater audiences, who marveled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes (‘X-Men‘ of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.

	“America was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.”
	

	“His farewell performance in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is yet to be seen,” McKellen concluded.

	Stewart and McKellen’s friendship was one of the most beloved in the entertainment industry. The two became friends while playing Professor X and Magneto, respectively, in 2000’s “X-Men.” Looking back in a 2020 interview with Wired, Stewart said, “We had adjoining trailers. On those kind of movies, you spend more time sitting in your trailer than you do in front of the camera. So Ian and I hung out together, drinking tea — and maybe, in the afternoon, something a little stronger — and we got to know one another, and the charm of it was that we found we had so much in common.”

	McKellen was the officiant when Stewart married his wife, Sunny Ozell, in 2013. “I’ll be frank with you — I’m in love with [him],” Stewart joked in the same interview. “But then, so is my wife in love with him, too, so that’s all right.” The friends made headlines several times over the years for so openly showing affection to each other, frequently kissing on the lips at red carpet events. 



	

					Ian McKellen, left and Patrick Stewart kiss at the U.K. premiere of McKellen’s film “Mr Holmes” in 2015.
									Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images
	



	In addition to the original “X-Men” in 2000, Stewart and McKellen starred in in the sequels “X2” (2003) and “X-Men: The Last Stand” (2006), then made a cameo in “The Wolverine” (2013) before fully reprising their roles in 2014’s “X-Men: Days of Future Past.” Stewart also starred in 2017’s “Logan,” and both appear in “Avengers: Doomsday,” which will be released this December.

	The pair has also worked together onstage, performing in a 2013 Broadway production of both Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” and Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” before doing “No Man’s Land” again in 2016 on London’s West End.

schema.headline: Ian McKellen Pays Tribute to Close Friend Patrick Stewart: ‘He Wore His Heart on His Sleeve’

title: What to Watch on Disney+ in November 2026
description: As Disney+ heads into November, the streaming platform is beginning to phase out of its Halloween thrills and introduce a new slate of holiday favor
body:
As Disney+ heads into November, the streaming platform is beginning to phase out of its Halloween thrills and introduce a new slate of holiday favorites. 
	Among this month’s Christmas-centered additions are “A Bad Moms Christmas,” “A Christmas Story,” “The Polar Express,” “Four Christmases” and “National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation,” all of which will be available to stream on Hulu for bundle subscribers. 

	“Percy Jackson and the Olympians” will return for its third season with a two-episode premiere, following Percy and his friend’s journey to stop the fall of Olympus. title: Todd Chrisley Didn't Initially 'Embrace' Savannah Dating Jason Galanis Due To Age-Gap
description:
Todd Chrisley
                          I Didn't Embrace Savannah's 27-Year Age Gap With Fiancé
body:
Todd Chrisley
                          I Didn't Embrace Savannah's 27-Year Age Gap With Fiancé
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 29, 2026
                
                            1:38 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 29, 2026
                                2:42 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Todd Chrisley wasn't initially a fan of his daughter Savannah Chrisley's relationship with fiancé Jason Galanis ... and it was all over their 27-year age gap.
      
    
            Todd told Bunnie Xo on her "Dumb Blonde" podcast Thursday ... things got to the point where he had to accept Savannah and Jason or "lose my daughter."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He added ... "And nothing is ever coming between me and my daughter. I love Savannah with my heart and soul, but did I advocate for this? No, but I will tell you that he has treated her with the utmost of respect."
      

            Todd revealed that after Jason asked for her hand in marriage, Todd told him ... "You do understand that she may be the only love that you claim you've ever had, but you won't be her only love."
      
    
            Apparently, Jason replied ... "Well, it's my job while I am to make sure she never forgets it."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Jason -- who is expecting a child with Savannah -- and Todd have quite a bit in common.
      
    
            Not only were they both recipients of clemency from President Donald Trump, but they also served hard time at the same prison, at the same time, for their federal fraud convictions.
      
    
            Todd's just a couple of years older than Jason ... so he won't be your typical son-in-law.

title: Elizabeth Holmes: Jerky From 'You Can See Everything' Has Major Spike in Sales
description:
Elizabeth Holmes
                          Fav Turkey Jerky Flying Off Shelves
body:
Elizabeth Holmes
                          Fav Turkey Jerky Flying Off Shelves
                          ... After Nathan Fielder Doc
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 29, 2026
                
                            1:30 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 29, 2026
                                2:06 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder aren't the only stars of "You Can See Everything" ... the turkey jerky brand the convicted felon chows down on in the film is also enjoying some time in the spotlight ... and getting a boost in sales.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... in the doc, Holmes eats Think Jerky at Federal Prison Camp Bryan, making it known it's her favorite food outside of her daily prison chow.
      
    
            The scene is apparently sticking in people's minds ... because TMZ has learned Think Jerky sales are skyrocketing as the movie does big numbers at the box office. We're told Sriracha Honey jerky sales are up 345% since the movie's release.
      
    
            A rep for Think Jerky tells TMZ … "We had absolutely no idea we were going to be in the movie, so the whole thing has been a bit of a whirlwind. We're a small, self-funded, employee-owned business that somehow ended up in one of the most talked-about films of the year."
      

            The rep tells us their jerky's fast becoming a pillar in pop culture ... sales are surging, jerky is selling out in stores, and people are dressing up as Think Jerky for Halloween.
      
    
            One flavor stands above all ... the film features Sriracha Honey Turkey Jerky -- created by Chicago chef Gale Gand -- and the brand says sales on Amazon have jumped 93%.
      
    
            Maybe you can see everything ... but Think Jerky certainly didn't see this exploding popularity coming!

                            5:55 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sir Ian McKellen was hit hard by the death of his close friend and collaborator, Sir Patrick Stewart ... mourning the loss of a legend.
      
    
            Ian remembered his friend saying, "He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The 'Lord of the Rings' star remembered meeting Patrick "half a century ago" ... however, his first strong memory of his friend was warning him not to take his now iconic 'Star Trek' -- believing it would put his prestigious stage career at risk.
      

            Ian went on to express gratitude on behalf of the "Trekkies" and "film and theatre audiences" who were able to marvel at his late friend's talents. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The iconic actors' friendship spans decades -- they both starred in "X-Men" together back in 2000.
      
    
            Ian even officiated Patrick's wedding to Sunny Ozell in a Mexican restaurant back in 2013.
      
    
            Patrick previously recalled the sweet, spontaneous ceremony on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," saying ... "We learned that [McKellen] could not use his [ministry] credentials in Nevada, which is where we were getting married … so we invited Ian and two of our guests and a [theater] director to a Mexican restaurant for dinner."
      
    
            As we previously reported, Patrick passed away at 86 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's.

NYC Driver

                          Multiple People Injured
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A driver in New York City hopped a curb and plowed into a Halloween event hosted by the NYPD ... injuring several people, including a child.
      
    
            The driver -- who New York Post reports is a 56-year-old man -- allegedly lost control of a black sedan and ran directly into a "Trunk or Treat" event Thursday outside the 83rd Precinct Station House in Brooklyn.
      
    
            Authorities told the outlet he also struck a private ambulance that was on scene in case of emergency.
      

        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            Reports differ ... with the New York Post noting 4 people -- including a child -- were injured, while CBS says 6 people sustained injuries. First responders checked on several others at the scene as well.
      
    
            Photos and video from the scene show the street corner thrown into chaos ... and the damaged ambulance.
      
    
            NYP reports the driver was taken into police custody ... and a breathalyzer test has been administered.
      
    
            Unclear exactly what caused the incident ... but the Post's sources are clear that a terrorist attack is not suspected at this time.
